answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with earned-trust rate limits: every new identity starts at the nadir of a trust ladder, allowed only a trickle of transactions, like a small wharf that admits one boat at a time. Quotas rise only after a long history of honest, settled work, so each fake identity faces the same slow climb. The delta between a fresh Sybil and a trusted agent is therefore measured in months of costly, verifiable behavior — creating thousands of identities buys an attacker almost nothing, because none of them can transact at scale.
